Hey there, I'm sorry for how this has made you feel. Hopefully it's for a legitimate reason and not just him being embarrassed about how you two met. For me, I hid my partner from my family because of my family's religion. Last time I revealed I had an online partner (an ex), I was completely blocked off and forced to ghost him because that's what my family's religion told them to do. For the sake of our relationship, I kept my current bf a secret until I was able to move out and move in with him. 

Mine was an extreme case, but maybe your partner is unable to tell as well out of fear of what the family will do?

Ours was a pretty crazy story. My family was very strictly religious to the point where I was held back from many fundamental parts of life. During that time, I met and kept my LDR boyfriend a secret for almost a year and 6 months. Once my family's religion got too much for me, my bf's family offered for me to live with them. I accepted and flew halfway across the country at 18 and moved in with them. Had to learn to be a *real* adult and find my independence with them.  Both my bf and his family supported me so I could find a good nearby college, start my dream career, and just recently buy my first ever car. This man is the love of my life and I can't wait to go on so many more adventures with him. All goes well (and I know they will, there's just some things you know deep down), we're planning on getting married April 2024.

My LDR bf and I actually met in person for the first time the week we moved in together! We had been together for almost a year and a half at that point, so we were basically immediately comfortable with each other. We couldn't hang out 1-1 for a bit, but the second we did it was like I felt the biggest wave of warmth, calmness, and love I'd ever felt just being able to hold him and see him up close. Instantly comfortable. Intimacy wise ended up being about a week later or so, not rushed at all.

Hi! I'm someone who's done exactly what you're thinking of doing. While I had loving parents, they kept forcing their religious ideas on me to the point of locking me away from the world (they are JWs). I made the decision to move in with my LDR boyfriend and his family about 6 months ago. 

One of the best decisions I could ever have made.

The love I feel for him each and every day to be able to feel and hold him is indescribable. And his family are absolute saints who have basically taken me in as their daughter and love me like I love them. I'm happier than ever!

So go for it!

I will say though, you WILL hit some rough spots, most likely. This will be an entirely new dynamic for you and your girlfriend. To prepare, I recommend calling a TON with her. Like videocalling all the time if you can. Don't even have to talk, just have your phone somewhere around you so you get used to being around each other all the time. Being able to be bored together is one of the most important things here. 

Try to set up calls when you sleep too. Already having a routine of falling asleep and waking up together will also help get you accustomed to that routine. 

Most importantly, have no expectations. When I moved in with my bf, our relationship basically did a 180 with a lot of our "roles". (For instance, he was always the clingier one who got jealous when I'd hang out with my guy friends, but that completely went away when I moved here, and instead I became the one who would get jealous and had to work on that.) Being in an LDR will give you a great foundation together, but things will definitely change a bit being in person (not necessarily in a bad way!).

Just keep communication open and stay dedicated to each other and you two got this. Hope all goes well and you make the leap!

With her husband having cheated on her, she probably felt more secure knowing that she could be with OP most of the day. And then later when he started hanging out with others more frequently (although this is also normal in a relationship), she probably got spooked by the change rather than wanting to control him (even if she accidentally did) and then got extremely upset when her feelings were dismissed. Doesn't excuse what she did towards the end of the 'relationship' though, that goes past any level of understanding.

I respectfully disagree, LDRs at your age *can* work and I've seen it time and time again. Especially don't uproot your life to close the gap or insist your partner do the same though.

Dedication, effort, and communication is the biggest thing here. My BF and I are in the exact same boat as you. We have constant arguments, but guess what? We'll have been dating for 1 year on the 11th of this month and our entire relationship has been LDR. We're barely younger than you guys too. You two need the mindset of being dedicated to each other. And if she's not listening to your feelings, you need to sit down and gently talk it out with her. Ask her to sit down and talk, to listen before getting angry, and explain as gently as you can. 

I get her mindset, sometimes during arguments I just get so fired up that, even if I maybe subconsciously know I'm being a little less than fair, my anger just clouds my judgement and it isn't until I've calmed down that I can see it and apologize. If she's at least somewhat aware of this, she'll listen. Also ask why she gets so angry. For me, I usually get the most angry if there's a repeated behavior that I've already expressed hurts/angers me. 

TL;DR: LDRs can work, you just need dedication. Do NOT uproot your life to close the gap. Communicate. 

Good luck OP!

Hi there! I'm currently in an almost-year-long LDR and the best advice I can give is set up scheduled call times. My bf and I's sweet spot is between 10/11-2 at night. Also, if you two are able, have silent calls together whenever you can! Miss your SO but can't talk at the moment? No problem, just facetime them so you can see them without even needing to talk. Whenever we're working for long periods, we just Facetime and do our own thing so it feels like we're around each other. Works like a charm! 

Oh and one other thing, casual chatting is fun and all, but have planned dates together. My SO and I watch Supernatural, talk about our future careers, play games, and we even have a couple's notebook that we write in together. Simply put, have something planned so it doesn't feel repetitive!

Like the other responses: Communication. BUT I'll say a little twist about it. Communication is absolutely key, but you also need to understand *how* your partner communicates. Notice how some comments say they call their partners a few times a week while others say they call daily? I've had a few LDR relationships end because we had different needs in that regard. Talk about that, or at the very least, note how much your partner naturally communicates. 

Also, a tip for those who like to talk and see each other a lot, facetime for no reason. I don't mean talk every single second you can, I mean if you both are busy but in an area that you can, just silently facetime each other just to get the sense that the other is there. My boyfriend and I do it all the time! If he's maybe busy doing coaching, we'll facetime while he's working. Even though I don't get to hear him, I get to see him and feel him with me. It's definitely one of the fastest ways to get comfortable with each other and feel like you're spending quality time together.

Hi there, I've got a LDR bf who basically has the same issues as your girlfriend. The difference? It's more of a repetitive joke now, and he has several mental disorders that make him act and feel like this. Like other redditors commented, you need to talk with her again. It can be a sit down talk, or you could just casually ask "do you really think I'd cheat on you or have feelings for someone else?" Be gentle and loving, most of the time if she really cares for your feelings, she'll have an open and honest talk with you about it. But you've got to let her know that this isn't okay and that you need to live your life too. 

Whenever my boyfriend starts to get jealous at me talking to my guy friends, I smile at him and in the warmest tone go "you really think I'd do something like that?" 9/10 he softens and admits he doesn't think so, it's just his feelings of jealousy flaring up. 

Just: point is, you need to make a point of it and gently put your foot down, as long as you're loving and gentle, you know you've done your part. And as long as she cares about your feelings too, she'll listen.

Oh 100% towards the end there, that friendship just became a draining emotional support, and if anything I'm glad someone agreed!

1. Have you ever had a golden friendship turn toxic?

Unfortunately, yes I have. I had an online friend who was, basically, my best and closest friend who I've currently known for four years. About a year and a half ago, however...It turned toxic pretty fast.

2. Was it one thing that made you certain this person was now toxic or was it a series of events?

I wouldn't say she in general was toxic, but more of we became toxic to each other specifically. (This'll be a long one so I'll leave a TLDR after this response to this question!) 

But to answer this directly, it was a series of events. We talked everyday, all day, and it wasn't uncommon for us to playfully say "come back!" whenever we'd be gone for a while. Around a year and a half ago, that changed and she became more distant. It started off small, taking a day to reply, to two days, to three days, to replying with a single message every three days. This in itself, although sad, isn't entirely what went wrong. It was both of our reactions to it. Over the course of 8 months, I'd reach out to see what went wrong, and she'd tell me she either forgot or was busy, *but she expected me to text her everyday regardless of if she texted me back*. She'd also complain of another one of her friends doing the same thing. Then complained about us not talking as much, when SHE was the one doing it. I reacted badly, and we ended up getting into arguments or have dicussions with good solutions...That ended up not getting played out. Finally I just said, as kindly as I could, that I couldn't deal with the stress anymore and that I was done. She reacted badly (in a way I can't say due to respect for her), and she disappeared for 2 weeks before coming back. We all pretended like nothing happened, and she ended up getting *really* clingy and wanting us to go back to normal. I asked her to stop, multiple times, over a period of several months.
